Shared Rules for Handler Pairs

This section sets out the standard approach for booking, checking, and caring for companion animals traveling with their handlers. The Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways gives clear guidance, keeps the process calm, and helps travelers prepare with confidence.

Handlers should bring accurate documents, pack the crate so the animal can stand and rest comfortably, and confirm that the pet remains settled before departure. The desk reviews basic travel details, checks that the carrier is suitable, and records any care notes that support safe handling. For cat travel, <<FACT F079>>. When the animal is a rabbit, <<FACT F064>>. Staff should treat both cases with the same steady attention and should explain any concern in simple terms.

A traveler may present more than one handler pair, and each pair must be listed clearly so the desk can match the pet, the crate, and the approved route. If the animal shows stress, the desk should advise the handler to stay nearby, speak softly, and avoid unnecessary changes to the carrier. Blue may be used as a sample reference in training notes only when a pet name is needed, but no name should appear on a live record unless it is supplied by the traveler. The cabin team monitors animals during flight, and the desk should pass along any relevant care notes before departure so the handoff is smooth.

If the paperwork is incomplete, the desk should pause the booking until the missing items are supplied. If the crate is damaged, poorly ventilated, or not secure, the traveler must be asked to replace it before acceptance. The desk should remain courteous and practical at every step, since most issues are resolved quickly when the guidance is clear.

For any case that falls outside standard handling, contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor at Aurelia Skyways.
